Subject: Chisel Health demo follow-up — perf gating, token budgets & POC next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. I wanted to capture the performance items and clear next steps so we can scope the POC correctly. TL;DR: we need your peak concurrency / RPS profile, a small sample of representative prompts, and confirmation on streaming vs batch behavior so we can size Dedicated capacity and propose an SLO matrix.

Key perf items we covered:
- Latency targets: conversational UI p95 target ~250–300ms for <512 token responses; longer analytic responses acceptable up to ~800ms with streaming enabled.
- Throughput & concurrency: you mentioned occasional spikes — please confirm expected sustained concurrency and short spikes (RPS).
- Context window: you described inputs often 200–400 tokens, but some clinical summaries will push input+output toward ~6k tokens total. We need exact worst-case examples.
- Streaming: live clinician assist requires server-sent events/streaming for partial outputs and token-level latency; this affects how we prioritize KV cache and batching.

Immediate asks (can you send by Mon?):
1) Peak concurrent sessions and 95th-percentile RPS during business hours (CSV or just numbers).
2) 6–10 sample prompts representative of the two main flows (triage chat and clinical-summary generation).
3) Any hard SLO you must meet (e.g., regulatory SLAs, internal SLA to clinicians).

Attachments:
- chisel_perf_matrix.xlsx — initial sizing assumptions and where latency/throughput tradeoffs land.
- mep_mutual_action_plan.docx — high-level POC milestones and success criteria.

Proposed POC cadence:
- Week 0: NDA + sample data + mutual action plan sign-off
- Week 1–2: baseline perf run (synthetic and replay) to validate token envelope and latency with streaming enabled
- Week 3–4: canary in your staging with traffic mirror

Priyom and Dev are on copy to scope the runtime/ops details. Happy to hop on a 30-min sync if it'd help.

—

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear write-up. Happy to confirm the numbers below and I attached a small sample set of prompts as promised (chisel_sample_prompts.json).

Answers:
- Peak concurrency: sustained ~60 concurrent inference sessions during business hours; short spikes up to ~140 concurrent for ~2–3 minute windows (during morning rounds).
- RPS: steady-state ~25 RPS; spike up to ~80 RPS briefly.
- Prompt sizes: triage chat average input 280 tokens, typical output 120–350 tokens; clinical summary flow: input ~4,500–5,200 tokens (we compress notes), outputs range 800–1,600 tokens. Worst-case combined token envelope we've seen ~6,800 tokens.
- Streaming: yes, clinician assist needs token-by-token streaming for the chat flow; clinical summary can be batch but faster is better.
- Hard SLOs: clinicians expect sub-500ms partial response starts for chat flows (so streaming-first token latency matters); we can tolerate higher latency for final summary.

Procurement: procurement lead (Sally) asked I get you a statement of work draft and our standard security questionnaire. She's reviewing the mutual action plan now. Expect a short procurement window but need to show viable perf numbers to justify Dedicated.

Let us know if you want additional prompt categories. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Nice detail from Mike — that worst-case ~6.8k envelope is helpful and pushes this into multi-stage handling territory. A few notes on tradeoffs and what we'd validate in Week 1: 

1) Token-envelope strategy:
- For chat (streaming-first): prioritize low-first-token latency by disabling heavy batching for conversational paths and using prefixed KV caching. We can target ~200–300ms first-token p95 on a tuned Dedicated pool for chat flows up to ~512 tokens.
- For clinical-summary (6k+): run generation in a separate pool optimized for high-memory and quantization-friendly kernels; expect end-to-end latency to be higher (~1–3s) but we can stream partial chunks if they want incremental tokens.

2) Autoscaling & canaries:
- Canary plan: ramp 10% traffic for 48h, validate p95 and error rate, then 50% for 24h before full.
- Autoscaler settings: aggressive scale-up on queue depth during spikes, with a conservative scale-down to avoid oscillation.

3) Fallbacks & hedges:
- Model variants: canonical (full-precision) vs q8/q4_0 variants for cost-sensitive paths; fallback logic if p95 > SLO for >2min.
- Circuit-breakers: short-circuit to a smaller-context summarizer for non-critical batch jobs.

4) Measurement: we'll instrument token-level tracing and per-route latency buckets; need Chisel to provide traffic mix and a replay context to run against staging.

Action items for the POC kickoff:
- Chisel: upload 10–20 sample sessions split by flow to the shared Drive (link in Vanessa's email).
- Chisel: confirm the procurement timeline and who signs the SOW.
- Redwood (Dev): prepare a baseline runbook and perf harness to replay prompts at 1x/5x peak.

I'll draft a short POC acceptance criteria doc and drop into the Drive. If they want stricter first-token p95 for chat (<200ms) we'll need to discuss Dedicated sizing and potential premium tier.

—
